title: In characteristics two and three, a bounded function with large Gowers U4 norm correlates quantitatively with a cubic phase, allowing a nonclassical cubic in characteristic two
difficulty: Even after the precise quantitative triaffine-correlation theorem, polynomial normal form, analytic/partition rank comparison and terminal U3 inverse theorem, the author must integrate non-classical multilinear forms by a full coefficient classification and build characteristic-specific symmetry corrections. A new diagonal bilinear defect argument in characteristic two and controlled subspace extensions preserve quantitative rank losses. The final Fourier conditioning, quadratic corrections and eight-phase cube remove those defects with explicit losses, leaving a sustained nonroutine argument beyond ordinary qualification Fourier analysis; the complete selected outcome is conservatively H2.

title: The probability that a uniform permutation has no cycles of length at most m equals its Poisson prediction with a uniform Brun–Hooley sieve error exponential in n divided by m
difficulty: After elementary inclusion--exclusion, harmonic sums, Stirling bounds and exact binomial moments, the human proof still designs a logarithmic hierarchy of cycle-length intervals and unequal even truncation orders under a shared total-length budget. Its main product and separate first-failure error product must be evaluated simultaneously and optimized through factorial tails to achieve the u log u minus u log log log u exponent uniformly. That multilevel sieve construction exceeds ordinary single-variable inclusion--exclusion, so the independent original no-small-cycle outcome is conservatively H1.

title: Every full-dimensional finite subset of real d-space for d at least four has difference set size at least the sharp coefficient two d minus two plus one over d minus one times its size, up to a dimension-dependent power-saving error
difficulty: After the precisely stated small-doubling line-cover theorem and classical dimensional sumset bounds, the author still couples induction on dimension with induction on the number of parallel fibers and separates the resulting difference-set pieces. The full new asymmetric sumset bound requires several structural compressions that preserve projection counts and force three canonical configurations, followed by all fiber-mass and dimension cases. Those constructions supply the extra one over d minus one in the main coefficient and control discarded points through a dimension-drop argument, leaving a nonroutine geometric-combinatorial proof beyond ordinary qualification sumset inequalities; the original main outcome is conservatively H1.
